ukberi-tibyan:24-24.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَقَدْ هَمَّتْ بِهِ وَهَمَّ بِهَا لَوْلَا أَنْ رَأَى بُرْهَانَ رَبِّهِ كَذَلِكَ لِنَصْرِفَ عَنْهُ السُّوءَ وَالْفَحْشَاءَ إِنَّهُ مِنْ عِبَادِنَا الْمُخْلَصِينَ (٢٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَوْلَا أَنْ رَأَى): the answer of «لَوْلَا» is omitted, its implied form being "لَهَمَّ بِهَا" ("he would have inclined to her"); on this view the pause is at وَلَقَدْ هَمَّتْ بِهِ. The meaning is that he did not incline to her.
It is also said: the implied form is "had he not seen the proof, he would have committed the sin".
(كَذَلِكَ): in the position of the nominative (rafʿ), i.e. "the matter is thus" (الْأَمْرُ كَذَلِكَ).
It is also said: in the position of the accusative (naṣb), i.e. "a seeing like that" (رُؤْيَةٌ كَذَلِكَ).
The lām in «لِنَصْرِفَ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the omitted element.
And (الْمُخْلَصِينَ) is read with kasra on the lām, i.e. "those who make their deeds sincere" (الْمُخْلِصِينَ أَعْمَالَهُمْ); and with fatḥa on it, i.e. "those whom Allah has made pure for His obedience".

ukberi-tibyan:25-25.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَاسْتَبَقَا الْبَابَ وَقَدَّتْ قَمِيصَهُ مِنْ دُبُرٍ وَأَلْفَيَا سَيِّدَهَا لَدَى الْبَابِ قَالَتْ مَا جَزَاءُ مَنْ أَرَادَ بِأَهْلِكَ سُوءًا إِلَّا أَنْ يُسْجَنَ أَوْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ (٢٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ دُبُرٍ): the majority read it with the genitive and tanwīn.
Among the irregular (shādhdh) readings it was read with three ḍammas and without tanwīn (مِنْ دُبُرُ); it is then indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma because it has been cut off from the genitive construct (iḍāfa). The original is "مِنْ دُبُرِهِ" and "قُبُلِهِ", and then what was done with قَبْلُ and بَعْدُ was done with it. This is weak, because the genitive construct is not necessary to it in the way that it is necessary to the adverbs (ẓurūf) that become indeclinable when cut off from the genitive construct.

ukberi-tibyan:29-29.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يُوسُفُ أَعْرِضْ عَنْ هَذَا وَاسْتَغْفِرِي لِذَنْبِكِ إِنَّكِ كُنْتِ مِنَ الْخَاطِئِينَ (٢٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يُوسُفُ أَعْرِضْ): the majority read it with ḍamma on the fāʾ, and the implied form is "يَا يُوسُفُ" ("O Yūsuf").
Al-Aʿmash read it with fatḥa; the more likely explanation is that he brought it out according to the original form of the one addressed in the vocative (munādā), as came in poetry:
يَا عَدِيًّا لَقَدْ وَقَتْكَ الْأَوَاقِي
("O ʿAdī, the protectors have indeed protected you")
It is also said: this reading was not accurately recorded from al-Aʿmash, and the more likely explanation is that he paused on the word and then joined it, treating the joining like the pause; so he threw the vowel of the hamza onto the fāʾ and dropped the hamza, and the word came to be pronounced (يُوسُفَ اعْرِضْ). This is like what has been reported: «اللَّهُ أَكْبَرَ اشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا. . .» — with joining and fatḥa.
Among the irregular readings it was also read with ḍamma on the fāʾ and with أَعْرَضَ in the form of the past verb; this is weak because of His saying «وَاسْتَغْفِرِي»; it would have been more fitting for it to be with fāʾ: «فَاسْتَغْفِرِي».

ukberi-tibyan:30-30.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالَ نِسْوَةٌ فِي الْمَدِينَةِ امْرَأَةُ الْعَزِيزِ تُرَاوِدُ فَتَاهَا عَنْ نَفْسِهِ قَدْ شَغَفَهَا حُبًّا إِنَّا لَنَرَاهَا فِي ضَلَالٍ مُبِينٍ (٣٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (نِسْوَةٌ): it is read with kasra on the nūn and with ḍamma; they are two dialectal forms.
The alif of «الْفَتَى» is converted from a yāʾ, because they say فَتَيَانِ; and الْفُتُوَّةُ is irregular (shādhdh).
(قَدْ شَغَفَهَا): it is read with ghayn, and it is from shaghāf al-qalb, which is the heart's covering (membrane). The meaning is that it reached the membrane of her heart, and that love of him came to enclose her heart as the membrane encloses it.
It is also read with ʿayn (شَعَفَهَا); it is from your saying "فُلَانٌ مَشْعُوفٌ بِكَذَا", i.e. "infatuated with it and passionately devoted to it".
And (حُبًّا) is a tamyīz (specification); the original is "قَدْ شَغَفَهَا حُبُّهُ" ("his love has smitten her"). The clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «تُرَاوِدُ» or from «الْفَتَى».

ukberi-tibyan:31-31.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ بِمَكْرِهِنَّ أَرْسَلَتْ إِلَيْهِنَّ وَأَعْتَدَتْ لَهُنَّ مُتَّكَأً وَآتَتْ كُلَّ وَاحِدَةٍ مِنْهُنَّ سِكِّينًا وَقَالَتِ اخْرُجْ عَلَيْهِنَّ فَلَمَّا رَأَيْنَهُ أَكْبَرْنَهُ وَقَطَّعْنَ أَيْدِيَهُنَّ وَقُلْنَ حَاشَ لِلَّهِ مَا هَذَا بَشَرًا إِنْ هَذَا إِلَّا مَلَكٌ كَرِيمٌ (٣١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَأَعْتَدَتْ): it is from al-ʿatād, which is the thing made ready for a matter.
(مُتَّكَأً): the majority read it with doubling (tashdīd) of the tāʾ and with hamza, without lengthening (madd). The original of the word is مُوتَكَأً, from تَوَكَّأْتُ ("I leaned"), and what is meant by it is the sitting place in which one reclines; the wāw was replaced by a tāʾ and assimilated.
It was read irregularly with lengthening and hamza (مُتَّكَاءً), the alif in it arising from the prolongation (ishbāʿ) of the fatḥa.
It is also read with tanwīn without hamza (مُتَّكًا); the explanation of it is that he replaced the hamza with an alif and then dropped it because of the tanwīn.
Ibn Jinnī said: it may be from أَوْكَيْتُ السِّقَاءَ ("I tied up the waterskin"); the alif would then be a replacement for the yāʾ, and its pattern would be mufta'al from that.
It is also read with the tāʾ undoubled and without hamza (مُتْكًا); and it is said: al-mutk is the citron (al-utrujj).
(حَاشَى لِلَّهِ): it is read with two alifs, and that is the original.
The majority hold that it is a verb here; they have said from it أُحَاشِي ("I except"); and this is supported by the entry of the lām on the name of Allah the Exalted: if it were a preposition, it would not enter upon a preposition. Its agent (fāʿil) is implied (muḍmar), its implied form being "حَاشَى يُوسُفُ", i.e. "Yūsuf kept far from sin out of fear of Allah".
The origin of the word is from حَاشَيْتُ الشَّيْءَ; so حَاشَى means "he went to a ḥāshiya", i.e. to one side.
It is also read without an alif after the shīn (حَاشَ); it was dropped for lightness, and in that the Muṣḥaf was followed; what made this acceptable is the frequency of its use.
It was read irregularly «حَشَا لِلَّهِ», without an alif after the ḥāʾ; it is a lightened form of it.
Some of them said: it is a preposition and the lām is redundant (zāʾida); this is weak, because the place for something like this is poetic necessity.
(مَا هَذَا بَشَرًا): it is read with fatḥa on the bāʾ, i.e. "a human being"; rather, he is an angel.
It is also read with kasra on the bāʾ (بِشِرًى), from al-shirāʾ ("buying"), i.e. "this was not obtained for a price". It may also be a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the passive participle (mafʿūl), i.e. "something bought"; and on this view «مَلِكٌ» was read with kasra on the lām ("a king").

ukberi-tibyan:33-33.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ رَبِّ السِّجْنُ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ مِمَّا يَدْعُونَنِي إِلَيْهِ وَإِلَّا تَصْرِفْ عَنِّي كَيْدَهُنَّ أَصْبُ إِلَيْهِنَّ وَأَكُنْ مِنَ الْجَاهِلِينَ (٣٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (رَبِّ السِّجْنُ): it is read with kasra on the sīn and ḍamma on the nūn; it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «أَحَبُّ» is its khabar (predicate). What is meant is the place of confinement, and the implied form is "living in the prison".
It is also read with fatḥa on the sīn (السَّجْنُ), as a maṣdar (verbal noun: "imprisonment").
It is also read «رَبُّ» with ḍamma on the bāʾ, without yāʾ, «وَالسِّجْنِ» with kasra on the sīn and the genitive by genitive construct, i.e. "the master of the prison"; and the implied form is "meeting him" or "enduring him".

ukberi-tibyan:35-35.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ثُمَّ بَدَا لَهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا رَأَوُا الْآيَاتِ لَيَسْجُنُنَّهُ حَتَّى حِينٍ (٣٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بَدَا لَهُمْ): concerning the agent (fāʿil) of «بَدَا» there are three views. The first: it is omitted, and (لَيَسْجُنُنَّهُ) stands in its place, i.e. "imprisonment appeared (fitting) to them"; it was omitted and the clause was put in its place; but the clause is not the agent, because clauses cannot be such. The second: the agent is implied (muḍmar), and it is the maṣdar of بَدَا, i.e. "an appearing (بَدَاءٌ) appeared to them", and it was left implied. The third: the agent is what the speech points to, i.e. "an opinion appeared to them" (بَدَا لَهُمْ رَأْيٌ), and it too was left implied. And (حَتَّى) is attached to «يَسْجُنُنَّهُ». And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:36-36.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَدَخَلَ مَعَهُ السِّجْنَ فَتَيَانِ قَالَ أَحَدُهُمَا إِنِّي أَرَانِي أَعْصِرُ خَمْرًا وَقَالَ الْآخَرُ إِنِّي أَرَانِي أَحْمِلُ فَوْقَ رَأْسِي خُبْزًا تَأْكُلُ الطَّيْرُ مِنْهُ نَبِّئْنَا بِتَأْوِيلِهِ إِنَّا نَرَاكَ مِنَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ (٣٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَدَخَلَ مَعَهُ السِّجْنَ): the majority read it with kasra on the sīn, and it was read with fatḥa on it (السَّجْنَ); the implied form is "the place of imprisonment" or "into the prison".
And (قَالَ) is resumptive (mustaʾnaf), because he did not tell that dream at the time of his entering; nor is it an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), because entering does not lead to the dream.
(فَوْقَ رَأْسِي): an adverb (ẓarf) of «أَحْمِلُ».
It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الْخُبْز». And «تَأْكُلُ» is an adjective (ṣifa) of it.

ukberi-tibyan:39-41.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا صَاحِبَيِ السِّجْنِ أَأَرْبَابٌ مُتَفَرِّقُونَ خَيْرٌ أَمِ اللَّهُ الْوَاحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ (٣٩) مَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ إِلَّا أَسْمَاءً سَمَّيْتُمُوهَا أَنْتُمْ وَآبَاؤُكُمْ مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ بِهَا مِنْ سُلْطَانٍ إِنِ الْحُكْمُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ أَمَرَ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوا إِلَّا إِيَّاهُ ذَلِكَ الدِّينُ الْقَيِّمُ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ (٤٠) يَاصَاحِبَيِ السِّجْنِ أَمَّا أَحَدُكُمَا فَيَسْقِي رَبَّهُ خَمْرًا وَأَمَّا الْآخَرُ فَيُصْلَبُ فَتَأْكُلُ الطَّيْرُ مِنْ رَأْسِهِ قُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ الَّذِي فِيهِ تَسْتَفْتِيَانِ (٤١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَمِ اللَّهُ الْوَاحِدُ): «أَمْ» here is the connected (muttaṣila) one.
(سَمَّيْتُمُوهَا): it takes two objects, and the second has been omitted, i.e. "you named them gods".
And «أَسْمَاءً» here means "things named", or "possessors of names", because a name is not worshipped.
(أَمَرَ أَلَّا): it may be resumptive (mustaʾnaf), or it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) with (قَدْ) intended along with it; but this is weak because of the weakness of what governs it.

ukberi-tibyan:42-42.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالَ لِلَّذِي ظَنَّ أَنَّهُ نَاجٍ مِنْهُمَا اذْكُرْنِي عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ فَأَنْسَاهُ الشَّيْطَانُ ذِكْرَ رَبِّهِ فَلَبِثَ فِي السِّجْنِ بِضْعَ سِنِينَ (٤٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْهُمَا): it may be an adjective (ṣifa) of «نَاجٍ», or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الَّذِي»; it is not attached to «نَاجٍ», because the meaning is not according to that.

ukberi-tibyan:43-43.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ إِنِّي أَرَى سَبْعَ بَقَرَاتٍ سِمَانٍ يَأْكُلُهُنَّ سَبْعٌ عِجَافٌ وَسَبْعَ سُنْبُلَاتٍ خُضْرٍ وَأُخَرَ يَابِسَاتٍ يَا أَيُّهَا الْمَلَأُ أَفْتُونِي فِي رُؤْيَايَ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ لِلرُّؤْيَا تَعْبُرُونَ (٤٣))
His saying, Exalted is He: (سِمَانٍ): an adjective (ṣifa) of «بَقَرَاتٍ». In (ordinary) speech it would be permissible to put it in the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of «سَبْعَ».
And (يَأْكُلُهُنَّ) is in the position of the genitive or the accusative, according to what we have mentioned. Likewise «خُضْرٍ».
(لِلرُّؤْيَا): the lām in it is redundant (zāʾida), strengthening the verb since its object has been put before it; it may be dropped outside the Qurʾān, because one says عَبَّرْتُ الرُّؤْيَا ("I interpreted the dream").

ukberi-tibyan:44-44.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالُوا أَضْغَاثُ أَحْلَامٍ وَمَا نَحْنُ بِتَأْوِيلِ الْأَحْلَامِ بِعَالِمِينَ (٤٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَضْغَاثُ أَحْلَامٍ): i.e. "these are…".
(بِتَأْوِيلِ الْأَحْلَامِ): i.e. "the interpretation of the jumbles of dreams (أَضْغَاثِ الْأَحْلَامِ)"; this is necessary, because they did not claim ignorance of interpreting dreams.

ukberi-tibyan:45-45.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالَ الَّذِي نَجَا مِنْهُمَا وَادَّكَرَ بَعْدَ أُمَّةٍ أَنَا أُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِتَأْوِيلِهِ فَأَرْسِلُونِ (٤٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (نَجَا مِنْهُمَا): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent pronoun; it is not a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). It may also be a ḥāl from «الَّذِي».
And (ادَّكَرَ): its original is اذْتَكَرَ; the dhāl was replaced by a dāl and the tāʾ by a dāl, and the first was assimilated into the second, so that the two letters come close.
It is read irregularly with a doubled dotted dhāl (اذَّكَرَ); its explanation is that he changed the tāʾ into a dhāl and assimilated.
His saying, Exalted is He: (بَعْدَ أُمَّةٍ): it is read with ḍamma on the hamza and with kasra on it, i.e. "a favour", namely his release from prison; it may also mean "a period of time".
It is also read with fatḥa on the hamza and the mīm and a hāʾ with tanwīn (أَمَهٍ); this is forgetfulness; one says: أَمِهَ يَأْمَهُ أَمَهًا.

ukberi-tibyan:47-47.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ تَزْرَعُونَ سَبْعَ سِنِينَ دَأَبًا فَمَا حَصَدْتُمْ فَذَرُوهُ فِي سُنْبُلِهِ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِمَّا تَأْكُلُونَ (٤٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (دَأَبًا): accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "you will toil persistently" (تَدْأَبُونَ); the speech points to it.
It is read with sukūn on the hamza and with fatḥa on it; the verb from it is دَأَبَ دَأْبًا and دَئِبَ دَأْبًا.
It is also read with an alif without hamza, by lightening (takhfīf).

ukberi-tibyan:49-49.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ثُمَّ يَأْتِي مِنْ بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ عَامٌ فِيهِ يُغَاثُ النَّاسُ وَفِيهِ يَعْصِرُونَ (٤٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَعْصِرُونَ): it is read with yāʾ and with tāʾ and with fatḥa; the object is omitted, i.e. "they press grapes", because of the abundance of fertility.
It is also read with ḍamma on the tāʾ and fatḥa on the ṣād (تُعْصَرُونَ), i.e. "you will be rained upon"; it is from His saying (مِنَ الْمُعْصِرَاتِ).

ukberi-tibyan:51-51.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ مَا خَطْبُكُنَّ إِذْ رَاوَدْتُنَّ يُوسُفَ عَنْ نَفْسِهِ قُلْنَ حَاشَ لِلَّهِ مَا عَلِمْنَا عَلَيْهِ مِنْ سُوءٍ قَالَتِ امْرَأَةُ الْعَزِيزِ الْآنَ حَصْحَصَ الْحَقُّ أَنَا رَاوَدْتُهُ عَنْ نَفْسِهِ وَإِنَّهُ لَمِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ (٥١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ رَاوَدْتُنَّ): what governs the adverb (ẓarf) is «خَطْبُكُنَّ»; it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) by which a grave matter has been named, and it governs by virtue of its meaning, because its meaning is "what did you intend?" or "what did you do?".

ukberi-tibyan:52-52.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ذَلِكَ لِيَعْلَمَ أَنِّي لَمْ أَخُنْهُ بِالْغَيْبِ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِي كَيْدَ الْخَائِنِينَ (٥٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (ذَلِكَ لِيَعْلَمَ): i.e. "the matter is that"; and the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, its implied form being "Allah made that manifest so that he may know".

ukberi-tibyan:53-53.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا أُبَرِّئُ نَفْسِي إِنَّ النَّفْسَ لَأَمَّارَةٌ بِالسُّوءِ إِلَّا مَا رَحِمَ رَبِّي إِنَّ رَبِّي غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ (٥٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَّا مَا رَحِمَ رَبِّي): concerning «مَا» there are two views:
The first: it is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), and its position is the accusative; the implied form is "the soul is indeed ever commanding evil, except at the time of my Lord's mercy". Its parallel is (وَدِيَةٌ مُسَلَّمَةٌ إِلَى أَهْلِهِ إِلَّا أَنْ يَصَّدَّقُوا), whose being in the accusative as an adverb (ẓarf) they have mentioned; it is like your saying "I did not stand except on Friday". The other view: that «مَا» means «مَنْ» ("whoever"); the implied form is "the soul commands evil, except for the one on whom my Lord has mercy", or "except a soul on which my Lord has mercy, for it does not command evil".

ukberi-tibyan:56-56.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَكَذَلِكَ مَكَّنَّا لِيُوسُفَ فِي الْأَرْضِ يَتَبَوَّأُ مِنْهَا حَيْثُ يَشَاءُ نُصِيبُ بِرَحْمَتِنَا مَنْ نَشَاءُ وَلَا نُضِيعُ أَجْرَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ (٥٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَتَبَوَّأُ مِنْهَا حَيْثُ يَشَاءُ): «حَيْثُ» is an adverb (ẓarf) of «يَتَبَوَّأُ». It may also be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and «مِنْهَا» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يَتَبَوَّأُ»; it may not be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «حَيْثُ», because «حَيْثُ» is not complete except with the muḍāf ilayhi, and putting the ḥāl before the muḍāf ilayhi is not permissible.
And (يَشَاءُ) with yāʾ: its agent (fāʿil) is the pronoun of Yūsuf. With nūn (نَشَاءُ): it is the pronoun of the name of Allah, by way of magnification. It may also be that its agent is the pronoun of Yūsuf, because his will is from the will of Allah.
The lām in «لِيُوسُفَ» is redundant (zāʾida), i.e. "We established Yūsuf".
It may also not be redundant, the object being omitted, i.e. "We established matters for Yūsuf".
And (يَتَبَوَّأُ) is a ḥāl from Yūsuf.

ukberi-tibyan:62-62.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالَ لِفِتْيَانِهِ اجْعَلُوا بِضَاعَتَهُمْ فِي رِحَالِهِمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَعْرِفُونَهَا إِذَا انْقَلَبُوا إِلَى أَهْلِهِمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ (٦٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لِفِتْيَتِهِ): it is read with tāʾ on the pattern fiʿla; it is a plural of paucity (jamʿ qilla) like صِبْيَةٌ. And with nūn (لِفِتْيَانِهِ), like غِلْمَانٌ, which is one of the plurals of multitude (jumūʿ al-kathra); on this view it occurs in the place of the plural of paucity.
(إِذَا انْقَلَبُوا): what governs «إِذَا» is «يَعْرِفُونَهَا».

ukberi-tibyan:63-63.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلَمَّا رَجَعُوا إِلَى أَبِيهِمْ قَالُوا يَا أَبَانَا مُنِعَ مِنَّا الْكَيْلُ فَأَرْسِلْ مَعَنَا أَخَانَا نَكْتَلْ وَإِنَّا لَهُ لَحَافِظُونَ (٦٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (نَكْتَلْ): it is read with nūn, because sending him is a cause of the measuring for the group. And with yāʾ (يَكْتَلْ), on the view that the agent is the brother; since he was the cause, the verb was attributed to him, so it is as if he is the one who measures for the group.

ukberi-tibyan:64-64.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ هَلْ آمَنُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ إِلَّا كَمَا أَمِنْتُكُمْ عَلَى أَخِيهِ مِنْ قَبْلُ فَاللَّهُ خَيْرٌ حَافِظًا وَهُوَ أَرْحَمُ الرَّاحِمِينَ (٦٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَّا كَمَا أَمِنْتُكُمْ): in the position of the accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a trusting like my trusting you with his brother".
(خَيْرٌ حَافِظًا): it is read with the alif, and it is a tamyīz (specification); something like this may be put in a genitive construct. It is also said: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
It is also read «حِفْظًا», and it is a tamyīz and nothing else.

ukberi-tibyan:65-65.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَمَّا فَتَحُوا مَتَاعَهُمْ وَجَدُوا بِضَاعَتَهُمْ رُدَّتْ إِلَيْهِمْ قَالُوا يَا أَبَانَا مَا نَبْغِي هَذِهِ بِضَاعَتُنَا رُدَّتْ إِلَيْنَا وَنَمِيرُ أَهْلَنَا وَنَحْفَظُ أَخَانَا وَنَزْدَادُ كَيْلَ بَعِيرٍ ذَلِكَ كَيْلٌ يَسِيرٌ (٦٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (رُدَّتْ): the majority read it with ḍamma on the rāʾ, and that is the original.
It is also read with kasra on it (رِدَّتْ); its explanation is that he transferred the kasra of the second radical (ʿayn) to the first radical (fāʾ), as was done in قِيلَ and بِيعَ; and the doubled verb (muḍāʿaf) resembles the weak verb (muʿtall).
(مَا نَبْغِي): «مَا» is interrogative, in the position of the accusative by «نَبْغِي». It may also be negating; then in (نَبْغِي) there are two views. The first: it means "we seek", so the object is omitted, i.e. "we do not seek wrongdoing". The second: that it is intransitive, meaning "we do not transgress".

ukberi-tibyan:66-66.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ لَنْ أُرْسِلَهُ مَعَكُمْ حَتَّى تُؤْتُونِ مَوْثِقًا مِنَ اللَّهِ لَتَأْتُنَّنِي بِهِ إِلَّا أَنْ يُحَاطَ بِكُمْ فَلَمَّا آتَوْهُ مَوْثِقَهُمْ قَالَ اللَّهُ عَلَى مَا نَقُولُ وَكِيلٌ (٦٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَتَأْتُنَّنِي بِهِ): it is the answer to an oath according to the meaning, because the covenant (al-mīthāq) means an oath.
(إِلَّا أَنْ يُحَاطَ): it is an exception from a different genus (istithnāʾ min ghayr al-jins).
It may also be from the same genus; the implied form would then be "you shall surely bring him to me in every circumstance except in the circumstance of your being surrounded".

ukberi-tibyan:68-68.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا مِنْ حَيْثُ أَمَرَهُمْ أَبُوهُمْ مَا كَانَ يُغْنِي عَنْهُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ إِلَّا حَاجَةً فِي نَفْسِ يَعْقُوبَ قَضَاهَا وَإِنَّهُ لَذُو عِلْمٍ لِمَا عَلَّمْنَاهُ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ (٦٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا مِنْ حَيْثُ أَمَرَهُمْ): concerning the answer of «لَمَّا» there are two views:
The first: it is «آوَى» (in the next verse), and it is the answer of the first «لَمَّا» and of the second, like your saying "when I came to you and when I spoke to you, you answered me". What made this acceptable is that their entering upon Yūsuf follows their entering through the gates.
The second: it is omitted, its implied form being "they complied", or "they fulfilled their father's need", and the like.
It may also be that the answer is the meaning of «مَا كَانَ يُغْنِي عَنْهُمْ».
And (حَاجَةً) is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and the agent (fāʿil) of «يُغْنِي» is "the dispersal" (التَّفَرُّقُ).

ukberi-tibyan:69-69.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا عَلَى يُوسُفَ آوَى إِلَيْهِ أَخَاهُ قَالَ إِنِّي أَنَا أَخُوكَ فَلَا تَبْتَئِسْ بِمَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ (٦٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قَالَ إِنِّي أَنَا): it is resumptive (mustaʾnaf); and likewise, everything that requires an answer, whose answer has been mentioned, and after which «قَالَ» then comes — it is resumptive.

ukberi-tibyan:72-75.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالُوا نَفْقِدُ صُوَاعَ الْمَلِكِ وَلِمَنْ جَاءَ بِهِ حِمْلُ بَعِيرٍ وَأَنَا بِهِ زَعِيمٌ (٧٢) قَالُوا تَاللَّهِ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتُمْ مَا جِئْنَا لِنُفْسِدَ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَمَا كُنَّا سَارِقِينَ (٧٣) قَالُوا فَمَا جَزَاؤُهُ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ كَاذِبِينَ (٧٤) قَالُوا جَزَاؤُهُ مَنْ وُجِدَ فِي رَحْلِهِ فَهُوَ جَزَاؤُهُ كَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي الظَّالِمِينَ (٧٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (صُوَاعَ الْمَلِكِ): the majority read it with ḍamma on the ṣād and an alif after the wāw.
It is also read without the alif; some of them put ḍamma on the ṣād (صُوعَ) and some put fatḥa on it (صَوْعَ).
It is also read «صَاعَ الْمَلِكِ». All of these are dialectal forms of it, and it is the vessel from which one drinks.
It is also read «صَوْغَ الْمَلِكِ», with a dotted ghayn, i.e. "the thing he had wrought (of metal)".
(قَالُوا جَزَاؤُهُ): there are three views on it:
The first: that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "its penalty with us is like its penalty with you"; the hāʾ refers back to the thief or to the theft, and the preceding speech gives evidence for both. On this view, His saying (مَنْ وُجِدَ) is a mubtadaʾ, «فَهُوَ» is a second mubtadaʾ, (جَزَاؤُهُ) is the khabar of the second mubtadaʾ, and the second mubtadaʾ with its khabar is the khabar of the first.
And (مَنْ) is conditional, and the fāʾ is its answer.
It may also mean «الَّذِي» ("the one who"), the fāʾ entering into its khabar because of the vagueness in it; the implied form is "the enslavement of the one in whose saddlebag it is found — it (i.e. the enslavement) is the penalty of the thief".
It may also be that the hāʾ in «جَزَاؤُهُ» refers to the theft.
The second view: that «جَزَاؤُهُ» is a mubtadaʾ and «مَنْ وُجِدَ» its khabar, the implied form being "the enslavement of the one in whose saddlebag it is found"; and «فَهُوَ جَزَاؤُهُ» is a mubtadaʾ and khabar emphasising the meaning of the first.
The third view: that «جَزَاؤُهُ» is a mubtadaʾ, «مَنْ وُجِدَ» a second mubtadaʾ, «فَهُوَ» a third mubtadaʾ, and «جَزَاؤُهُ» the khabar of the third; the referent pronoun (ʿāʾid) back to the first mubtadaʾ is the last hāʾ, and back to the second it is «هُوَ».
(كَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي): the kāf is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "a recompense like that".

ukberi-tibyan:76-76.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَبَدَأَ بِأَوْعِيَتِهِمْ قَبْلَ وِعَاءِ أَخِيهِ ثُمَّ اسْتَخْرَجَهَا مِنْ وِعَاءِ أَخِيهِ كَذَلِكَ كِدْنَا لِيُوسُفَ مَا كَانَ لِيَأْخُذَ أَخَاهُ فِي دِينِ الْمَلِكِ إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ اللَّهُ نَرْفَعُ دَرَجَاتٍ مَنْ نَشَاءُ وَفَوْقَ كُلِّ ذِي عِلْمٍ عَلِيمٌ (٧٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وِعَاءِ أَخِيهِ): the majority read it with kasra on the wāw, and that is the original, because it is from وَعَى يَعِي ("to contain").
It is also read with hamza (إِعَاءِ), the hamza being a replacement for the wāw; they are two dialectal forms; one says وِعَاءٌ and إِعَاءٌ, وِشَاحٌ and إِشَاحٌ, وِسَادَةٌ and إِسَادَةٌ. They resorted to the hamza only because of the heaviness of the kasra on the wāw.
It is also read with ḍamma on it (وُعَاءِ), and that is a dialectal form.
If it is asked: why did He not say "فَاسْتَخْرَجَهَا مِنْهُ" ("then he took it out of it"), since it had already been mentioned? It is answered: He had not explicitly stated the searching of his brother's bag so as to refer back to it with a pronoun; so He mentioned it overtly, so that this would be a pointer to what is omitted; its implied form is "then he searched his brother's bag and took it out of it".
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَذَلِكَ كِدْنَا), (إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ) and (دَرَجَاتٍ مَنْ نَشَاءُ): all of this has already been mentioned.
(وَفَوْقَ كُلِّ ذِي عِلْمٍ عَلِيمٌ): it is read irregularly «ذِي عَالِمٍ», and there are three views on it:
The first: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), like الْبَاطِلُ. The second: «ذِي» is redundant (zāʾida); the like of that has come in poetry, as in the saying of al-Kumayt:
إِلَيْكُمْ ذَوِي آلِ النَّبِيِّ
("To you, O family of the Prophet")
The third: that he put the name in a genitive construct with the thing named, which is omitted, its implied form being "possessor of what is named 'knower'", as in the saying of the poet:
إِلَى الْحَوْلِ ثُمَّ اسْمُ السَّلَامِ عَلَيْكُمَا
("Until the year is out; then the name of peace be upon you both")

ukberi-tibyan:77-77.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالُوا إِنْ يَسْرِقْ فَقَدْ سَرَقَ أَخٌ لَهُ مِنْ قَبْلُ فَأَسَرَّهَا يُوسُفُ فِي نَفْسِهِ وَلَمْ يُبْدِهَا لَهُمْ قَالَ أَنْتُمْ شَرٌّ مَكَانًا وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا تَصِفُونَ (٧٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَأَسَرَّهَا): the pronoun refers back to their attributing theft to him; the speech has pointed to it.
It is also said: there is a fronting and postponing (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr) in the speech, its implied form being "he said within himself: you are worse in position"; and «أَسَرَّهَا», i.e. this statement.
And (مَكَانًا) is a tamyīz (specification), i.e. "worse than him" or "than the two of them".

ukberi-tibyan:78-78.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالُوا يَا أَيُّهَا الْعَزِيزُ إِنَّ لَهُ أَبًا شَيْخًا كَبِيرًا فَخُذْ أَحَدَنَا مَكَانَهُ إِنَّا نَرَاكَ مِنَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ (٧٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَخُذْ أَحَدَنَا مَكَانَهُ): it (مَكَانَهُ) is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), and what governs it is «خُذْ».
It may also be construed according to the meaning, i.e. "put one of us in his place".

ukberi-tibyan:79-79.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ مَعَاذَ اللَّهِ أَنْ نَأْخُذَ إِلَّا مَنْ وَجَدْنَا مَتَاعَنَا عِنْدَهُ إِنَّا إِذًا لَظَالِمُونَ (٧٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَعَاذَ اللَّهِ): it is a maṣdar (verbal noun); the implied form is "from that we should take" (مِنْ أَنْ نَأْخُذَ).

ukberi-tibyan:80-80.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلَمَّا اسْتَيْأَسُوا مِنْهُ خَلَصُوا نَجِيًّا قَالَ كَبِيرُهُمْ أَلَمْ تَعْلَمُوا أَنَّ أَبَاكُمْ قَدْ أَخَذَ عَلَيْكُمْ مَوْثِقًا مِنَ اللَّهِ وَمِنْ قَبْلُ مَا فَرَّطْتُمْ فِي يُوسُفَ فَلَنْ أَبْرَحَ الْأَرْضَ حَتَّى يَأْذَنَ لِي أَبِي أَوْ يَحْكُمَ اللَّهُ لِي وَهُوَ خَيْرُ الْحَاكِمِينَ (٨٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (اسْتَيْأَسُوا): it is read with a yāʾ followed by a hamza; it is from يَئِسَ ("to despair").
It is also read اسْتَيْأَسُوا with an alif after the tāʾ and before the yāʾ (اسْتَايَسُوا); it is a metathesised form (maqlūb): one says يَئِسَ and أَيِسَ, and the original is with the yāʾ first, and the inflection of the word follows that. As for «إِيَاسٌ», the name of a man, it is not the maṣdar of this verb; rather it is the maṣdar of أُسْتُهُ, i.e. "I gave him". However, the hamza in the verse was changed into an alif for lightening.
[Translator's note: the source writes the second reading with the same spelling اسْتَيْأَسُوا as the first, while describing it as having an alif after the tāʾ; the form described is اسْتَايَسُوا.]
(نَجِيًّا): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent pronoun in «خَلَصُوا»; it is a singular in the place of a plural, i.e. "confidants" (أَنْجِيَةٌ), as Allah the Exalted said: (ثُمَّ نُخْرِجُكُمْ طِفْلًا).
And (مِنْ قَبْلُ): i.e. "and before that".
(مَا فَرَّطْتُمْ): concerning «مَا» there are two views. The first: it is redundant (zāʾida), and «مِنْ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb, i.e. "and you fell short before". The second: it is maṣdariyya, and concerning its position there are three views. The first: nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with «مِنْ قَبْلُ» its khabar (predicate), i.e. "and your falling short regarding Yūsuf was before". This is weak, because «قَبْلُ», when it occurs as a khabar or a ṣila, is not cut off from the genitive construct, lest it remain incomplete. The second: its position is accusative, conjoined to what «تَعْلَمُوا» governs; its implied form is "did you not know your father's taking the covenant from you and your falling short regarding Yūsuf?". The third: it is conjoined to the noun of «إِنَّ», its implied form being "and that your falling short before regarding Yūsuf…".
It is also said: it is weak on these two views, because in them there is a separation between the conjunction and the maʿṭūf (conjoined); but we have made clear in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ that this is of no account.
As for the khabar of «إِنَّ» on the last view, it may be «فِي يُوسُفَ», and this is preferable so that «مِنْ قَبْلُ» is not made the khabar.
(فَلَنْ أَبْرَحَ الْأَرْضَ): it (الْأَرْضَ) is the object of «أَبْرَحَ», i.e. "I will not leave"; it may also be an adverb (ẓarf).

ukberi-tibyan:81-81.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ارْجِعُوا إِلَى أَبِيكُمْ فَقُولُوا يَا أَبَانَا إِنَّ ابْنَكَ سَرَقَ وَمَا شَهِدْنَا إِلَّا بِمَا عَلِمْنَا وَمَا كُنَّا لِلْغَيْبِ حَافِظِينَ (٨١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (سَرَقَ): it is read with fatḥa and without doubling, i.e. "according to what appeared to us".
It is also read with ḍamma on the sīn and doubling of the rāʾ with kasra on it (سُرِّقَ), i.e. "he was accused of theft".

ukberi-tibyan:82-82.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَاسْأَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ الَّتِي كُنَّا فِيهَا وَالْعِيرَ الَّتِي أَقْبَلْنَا فِيهَا وَإِنَّا لَصَادِقُونَ (٨٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَاسْأَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ): i.e. "the people of the town"; dropping the muḍāf was permissible because the meaning is not ambiguous.
As for His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالْعِيرَ الَّتِي. . . (٨٢)), what is meant by it is the camels; on this view the muḍāf is likewise omitted, i.e. "the owners of the caravan". It is also said: al-ʿīr is the caravan, i.e. the people returning from travel; on this view there is no omission in it.

ukberi-tibyan:84-84.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَتَوَلَّى عَنْهُمْ وَقَالَ يَا أَسَفَى عَلَى يُوسُفَ وَابْيَضَّتْ عَيْنَاهُ مِنَ الْحُزْنِ فَهُوَ كَظِيمٌ (٨٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَا أَسَفَى): the alif is a replacement for the yāʾ of the first person; the original is أَسَفِي; the fāʾ was given fatḥa and the yāʾ was turned into an alif, so that the voice with it would be fuller.
And (عَلَى) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «أَسَفَى».

ukberi-tibyan:85-85.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالُوا تَاللَّهِ تَفْتَأُ تَذْكُرُ يُوسُفَ حَتَّى تَكُونَ حَرَضًا أَوْ تَكُونَ مِنَ الْهَالِكِينَ (٨٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (تَفْتَأُ): i.e. «لَا تَفْتَأُ» ("you will not cease"); the «لَا» was dropped because it is known.
And (تَذْكُرُ) is in the position of the accusative as the khabar (predicate) of «تَفْتَأُ».

ukberi-tibyan:87-87.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا بَنِيَّ اذْهَبُوا فَتَحَسَّسُوا مِنْ يُوسُفَ وَأَخِيهِ وَلَا تَيْأَسُوا مِنْ رَوْحِ اللَّهِ إِنَّهُ لَا يَيْئَسُ مِنْ رَوْحِ اللَّهِ إِلَّا الْقَوْمُ الْكَافِرُونَ (٨٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ رَوْحِ اللَّهِ): the majority read it with fatḥa on the rāʾ; it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) meaning "mercy", except that the use of the verb from it is rare; it is used only with augmentation, such as أَرَاحَ and رَوَّحَ.
It is also read with ḍamma on the rāʾ (رُوحِ), and that is a dialectal form of it. It is also said: it is a noun standing for the maṣdar (ism maṣdar), like الشَّرْبُ and الشُّرْبُ.

ukberi-tibyan:88-88.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا عَلَيْهِ قَالُوا يَا أَيُّهَا الْعَزِيزُ مَسَّنَا وَأَهْلَنَا الضُّرُّ وَجِئْنَا بِبِضَاعَةٍ مُزْجَاةٍ فَأَوْفِ لَنَا الْكَيْلَ وَتَصَدَّقْ عَلَيْنَا إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَجْزِي الْمُتَصَدِّقِينَ (٨٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مُزْجَاةٍ): its alif is converted from a yāʾ or from a wāw, because they say زَجَا الْأَمْرُ يَزْجُو.
(فَأَوْفِ لَنَا الْكَيْلَ): i.e. "what is measured".

ukberi-tibyan:90-90.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالُوا أَئِنَّكَ لَأَنْتَ يُوسُفُ قَالَ أَنَا يُوسُفُ وَهَذَا أَخِي قَدْ مَنَّ اللَّهُ عَلَيْنَا إِنَّهُ مَنْ يَتَّقِ وَيَصْبِرْ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُضِيعُ أَجْرَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ (٩٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قَدْ مَنَّ اللَّهُ عَلَيْنَا): a resumptive clause (jumla mustaʾnafa). It is also said: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «يُوسُفُ» and «أَخِي»; but this is far-fetched because of the absence of something governing the ḥāl: «أَنَا» does not govern a ḥāl, and «هَذَا» cannot govern it, because it points to one person, while «عَلَيْنَا» refers back to both of them together.
(مَنْ يَتَّقِ): the majority read it with the yāʾ dropped; «مَنْ» is conditional and the fāʾ is its answer.
It is also read with the yāʾ (يَتَّقِي), and there are three views on it. The first: that he prolonged the kasra of the qāf, so the yāʾ arose.
The second: that he treated the vowel on the yāʾ as implied and dropped it by the jussive, treating the weak letter like a sound letter in that. The third: that he made «مَنْ» mean «الَّذِي»; on this view the verb is nominative (marfūʿ).
And (يَصْبِرْ) — with sukūn — has two explanations. The first: that he dropped the ḍamma so that the vowels would not follow one another in succession, or he intended a pause on it and treated the joining like the pause. The second: it is jussive (majzūm) according to the meaning, because «مَنْ» here, even though it means «الَّذِي», still carries the sense of a condition because of the generality and vagueness in it; and that is why the fāʾ entered its khabar. Its parallel is «فَأَصَّدَّقَ وَأَكُنْ» in the reading of those who read it in the jussive.
The referent pronoun (ʿāʾid) from the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "the doers of good among them".
It may also be that he put the overt noun in place of the pronoun, i.e. "We do not let their reward be lost".

ukberi-tibyan:92-92.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ لَا تَثْرِيبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْيَوْمَ يَغْفِرُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ وَهُوَ أَرْحَمُ الرَّاحِمِينَ (٩٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَا تَثْرِيبَ): concerning the khabar (predicate) of «لَا» there are two views. The first: His saying «عَلَيْكُمُ»; on this view «الْيَوْمَ» is accusative by the khabar. It is also said: «الْيَوْمَ» is accusative by «يَغْفِرُ». The second: the khabar is «الْيَوْمَ», and «عَلَيْكُمُ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the adverb or to what governs the adverb, which is "being settled" (al-istiqrār).
It is also said: it is for clarification (tabyīn), like the lām in their saying سَقْيًا لَكَ ("may you be watered"). «عَلَى» may not be attached to «تَثْرِيبَ», nor may «الْيَوْمَ» be accusative by it, because the noun of «لَا», when it governs, takes tanwīn.

ukberi-tibyan:93-93.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (اذْهَبُوا بِقَمِيصِي هَذَا فَأَلْقُوهُ عَلَى وَجْهِ أَبِي يَأْتِ بَصِيرًا وَأْتُونِي بِأَهْلِكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ (٩٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِقَمِيصِي): it may be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "carry my shirt"; it may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "go, with my shirt with you".
And (بَصِيرًا) is a ḥāl in both places.

ukberi-tibyan:100-100.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَرَفَعَ أَبَوَيْهِ عَلَى الْعَرْشِ وَخَرُّوا لَهُ سُجَّدًا وَقَالَ يَا أَبَتِ هَذَا تَأْوِيلُ رُؤْيَايَ مِنْ قَبْلُ قَدْ جَعَلَهَا رَبِّي حَقًّا وَقَدْ أَحْسَنَ بِي إِذْ أَخْرَجَنِي مِنَ السِّجْنِ وَجَاءَ بِكُمْ مِنَ الْبَدْوِ مِنْ بَعْدِ أَنْ نَزَغَ الشَّيْطَانُ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَ إِخْوَتِي إِنَّ رَبِّي لَطِيفٌ لِمَا يَشَاءُ إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْعَلِيمُ الْحَكِيمُ (١٠٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (سُجَّدًا): an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), because the prostration comes after the falling down.
(رُؤْيَايَ مِنْ قَبْلُ): the adverb is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «رُؤْيَايَ», because the meaning is "my dream that was before"; and what governs it is «هَذَا».
It may also be an adverb (ẓarf) of the dream, i.e. "the interpretation of my dream at that time".
It may also be that what governs it is «تَأْوِيلُ», because the interpretation was thus from the time it occurred, and now it has become manifest to him.
And (قَدْ جَعَلَهَا) is an anticipated ḥāl; it may also be a concurrent one (muqārina).
And (حَقًّا) is the adjective of a maṣdar, i.e. "a true making".
It may also be a second object, with «جَعَلَ» meaning "made into" (صَيَّرَ). It may also be a ḥāl, i.e. "He set it down as sound".
It may also be that «حَقًّا» is a maṣdar not from the wording of the verb but from its meaning, because «جَعَلَهَا» has the meaning of "He realised it" (حَقَّقَهَا), and «حَقًّا» has the meaning of "realisation" (تَحْقِيق).
And (وَقَدْ أَحْسَنَ بِي): it is said that the bāʾ means «إِلَى» ("to"). It is also said: it has its usual meaning and the object is omitted, its implied form being "and He has done His work well with me".
And (إِذْ) is an adverb (ẓarf) of «أَحْسَنَ», or of "His work".

ukberi-tibyan:101-101.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (رَبِّ قَدْ آتَيْتَنِي مِنَ الْمُلْكِ وَعَلَّمْتَنِي مِنْ تَأْوِيلِ الْأَحَادِيثِ فَاطِرَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ أَنْتَ وَلِيِّي فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ تَوَفَّنِي مُسْلِمًا وَأَلْحِقْنِي بِالصَّالِحِينَ (١٠١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنَ الْمُلْكِ) and «مِنْ تَأْوِيلِ الْأَحَادِيثِ»: it is said that the object is omitted, i.e. "something great of sovereignty" and "a share of interpretation".
It is also said: it («مِنْ») is redundant (zāʾida). It is also said: «مِنْ» is for explaining the genus (bayān al-jins).

ukberi-tibyan:105-109.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ آيَةٍ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ يَمُرُّونَ عَلَيْهَا وَهُمْ عَنْهَا مُعْرِضُونَ وَمَا يُؤْمِنُ أَكْثَرُهُمْ بِاللَّهِ إِلَّا وَهُمْ مُشْرِكُونَ (١٠٦) أَفَأَمِنُوا أَنْ تَأْتِيَهُمْ غَاشِيَةٌ مِنْ عَذَابِ اللَّهِ أَوْ تَأْتِيَهُمُ السَّاعَةُ بَغْتَةً وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ (١٠٧) قُلْ هَذِهِ سَبِيلِي أَدْعُو إِلَى اللَّهِ عَلَى بَصِيرَةٍ أَنَا وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَنِي وَسُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَمَا أَنَا مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ (١٠٨) وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا مِنْ قَبْلِكَ إِلَّا رِجَالًا نُوحِي إِلَيْهِمْ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْقُرَى أَفَلَمْ يَسِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَيَنْظُرُوا كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ وَلَدَارُ الْآخِرَةِ خَيْرٌ لِلَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ (١٠٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالْأَرْضِ يَمُرُّونَ): the majority read it with the genitive, conjoined to «السَّمَاوَاتِ»; the pronoun in «عَلَيْهَا» is for the sign. It is also said: for the earth; then «يَمُرُّونَ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it; it is also said: from it and from the heavens.
The meaning of «يَمُرُّونَ» is "they witness" or "they know". It is also read «وَالْأَرْضَ» with the accusative, i.e. "and they traverse the earth", «يَمُرُّونَ» explaining (the omitted verb).
It is also read with the nominative (وَالْأَرْضُ), as a mubtadaʾ (subject).
And (بَغْتَةً) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl.
And (أَدْعُو إِلَى اللَّهِ) is resumptive (mustaʾnaf). It is also said: a ḥāl from the yāʾ.
And (عَلَى بَصِيرَةٍ) is a ḥāl, i.e. "being certain".
And (وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَنِي) is conjoined to the agent pronoun in «أَدْعُو».
It may also be a mubtadaʾ, i.e. "and whoever follows me is likewise".
And (مِنْ أَهْلِ الْقُرَى) is an adjective (ṣifa) of «رِجَالًا», or a ḥāl from the genitive pronoun (in «إِلَيْهِمْ»).

ukberi-tibyan:110-110.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (حَتَّى إِذَا اسْتَيْأَسَ الرُّسُلُ وَظَنُّوا أَنَّهُمْ قَدْ كُذِبُوا جَاءَهُمْ نَصْرُنَا فَنُجِّيَ مَنْ نَشَاءُ وَلَا يُرَدُّ بَأْسُنَا عَنِ الْقَوْمِ الْمُجْرِمِينَ (١١٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قَدْ كُذِبُوا): it is read with ḍamma on the kāf and doubling of the dhāl with kasra on it (كُذِّبُوا), i.e. "they knew that they had been charged with lying".
It is also said: the pronoun refers back to those to whom the messengers were sent, i.e. "the nations knew that the messengers had given them the lie".
It is also read with the dhāl undoubled (كُذِبُوا); on this view what is meant is the nations and nothing else.
It is also read with fatḥa and doubling (كَذَّبُوا), i.e. "and the messengers thought that the nations had given them the lie".
It is also read without doubling (كَذَبُوا), i.e. "the messengers knew that the nations had lied in what they claimed".
(فَنُنْجِي): it is read with two nūns and the jīm undoubled.
It is also read with a single nūn and doubling of the jīm (فَنُجِّيَ), as a past verb whose agent is not named (passive).
It is also read likewise but with sukūn on the yāʾ (فَنُجِّي); there are two explanations of it. The first: that he changed the second nūn into a jīm and assimilated it; on this view it is an imperfect (future). The second: that it is a past verb, and he gave sukūn to the yāʾ because of its heaviness with its vowel and the kasra of what precedes it.

ukberi-tibyan:111-111.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَقَدْ كَانَ فِي قَصَصِهِمْ عِبْرَةٌ لِأُولِي الْأَلْبَابِ مَا كَانَ حَدِيثًا يُفْتَرَى وَلَكِنْ تَصْدِيقَ الَّذِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَتَفْصِيلَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَهُدًى وَرَحْمَةً لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ (١٢١)).
[Translator's note: the verse number appears in the source as (١٢١); the verse is 111.]
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَا كَانَ حَدِيثًا): i.e. "the story of Yūsuf was not…", or "what is recited to them was not…".
(وَلَكِنْ تَصْدِيقَ): it has already been mentioned in Yūnus.
(وَهُدًى وَرَحْمَةً): both are conjoined to it. And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الر تِلْكَ آيَاتُ الْكِتَابِ الْمُبِينِ (١))
His saying (تِلْكَ آيَاتُ الْكِتَابِ): this has been mentioned at the beginning of Yūnus.

ukberi-tibyan:10-10.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ قَائِلٌ مِنْهُمْ لَا تَقْتُلُوا يُوسُفَ وَأَلْقُوهُ فِي غَيَابَةِ الْجُبِّ يَلْتَقِطْهُ بَعْضُ السَّيَّارَةِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ فَاعِلِينَ (١٠))
His saying (غَيَابَةِ الْجُبِّ): it is read with an alif after the yāʾ and the bāʾ undoubled; it is the place that hides whoever is in it.
It is also read in the plural, either because it is pluralized together with what surrounds it, as the poet said:
يَزِلُّ الْغُلَامُ الْخِفُّ عَنْ صَهَوَاتِهِ
(The light youth slips off its backs [i.e. the horse's back, pluralized with its surroundings])
or because there are places of that kind in the well. There are other readings of it that are evident, which we have not lengthened (the discussion) by mentioning.
(يَلْتَقِطْهُ): the majority read it with the yāʾ, construing it according to the wording of بَعْضُ.
It is also read with the tāʾ, construing it according to the meaning, since some of the caravan is a caravan; of this is their saying ذَهَبَتْ بَعْضُ أَصَابِعِهِ ("some of his fingers were lost", with a feminine verb).

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالُوا يَا أَبَانَا مَا لَكَ لَا تَأْمَنَّا عَلَى يُوسُفَ وَإِنَّا لَهُ لَنَاصِحُونَ (١١))
His saying (لَا تَأْمَنَّا): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).
The majority indicate the ḍamma of the first nūn. Some of them pronounce the ḍamma furtively (ikhtilās), so that it is perceived by hearing; some indicate it by rounding the lips, so that it is not perceived by hearing (ishmām); some assimilate it without rounding; and among the irregular (shādhdh) readings is one who pronounces the nūn distinctly, which is the analogical (form).

ukberi-tibyan:12-12.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَرْسِلْهُ مَعَنَا غَدًا يَرْتَعْ وَيَلْعَبْ وَإِنَّا لَهُ لَحَافِظُونَ (١٢))
His saying (نَرْتَعْ): the majority hold that the ʿayn is the last letter of the verb, its past being رَتَعَ. Some of them make it quiescent as the answer (to the imperative); some give it ḍamma, on the basis that it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara). Some read it with the nūn, and some read it with the yāʾ.
It is also read نَرْتَعِ with kasra on the ʿayn, being the pattern yaftaʿil from رَعَى ("to graze"), i.e. "our livestock will graze", or "we will eat".

ukberi-tibyan:14-14.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالُوا لَئِنْ أَكَلَهُ الذِّئْبُ وَنَحْنُ عُصْبَةٌ إِنَّا إِذًا لَخَاسِرُونَ (١٤))
His saying (وَنَحْنُ عُصْبَةٌ): the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
It was read, as an irregular (shādhdh) reading, «عُصْبَةً» in the accusative, and this is far-fetched. Its justification is that he omitted the khabar (predicate) and made this accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. "while we band together", or "gather as a band".

ukberi-tibyan:15-15.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلَمَّا ذَهَبُوا بِهِ وَأَجْمَعُوا أَنْ يَجْعَلُوهُ فِي غَيَابَةِ الْجُبِّ وَأَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْهِ لَتُنَبِّئَنَّهُمْ بِأَمْرِهِمْ هَذَا وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ (١٥))
His saying (فَلَمَّا ذَهَبُوا): the answer of «لَمَّا» is omitted, its implied form being "We made it known to him", or something similar. According to the view of the Kufans the answer is «أَوْحَيْنَا», and the wāw is redundant (zāʾida).
And (أَجْمَعُوا): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), with «قَدْ» intended along with it, or it may be maʿṭūf (conjoined).

ukberi-tibyan:16-16.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَجَاءُوا أَبَاهُمْ عِشَاءً يَبْكُونَ (١٦))
His saying (عِشَاءً): in it there are two views:
The first: it is an adverb (ẓarf), i.e. "at the time of evening", and «يَبْكُونَ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial). The second: it is the plural of عَاشٍ ("one night-blind"), like قَائِمٌ and قِيَامٌ.
It is also read with ḍamma on the ʿayn; the origin is عُشَاةٌ, like غَازٍ and غُزَاةٌ; the hāʾ was dropped and the alif added as compensation for it, then the alif was changed into a hamza.
There is discussion of this which we have mentioned in Āl ʿImrān at His saying, Glorified is He, (أَوْ كَانُوا غُزًّى).
It is also possible that he made fāʿil plural on fiʿāl, just as faʿīl is made plural on fiʿāl, because of the closeness between kasra and ḍamma.
It may also be like تُؤَامٌ and رُبَابٌ, and this is irregular (shādhdh).

ukberi-tibyan:18-18.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَجَاءُوا عَلَى قَمِيصِهِ بِدَمٍ كَذِبٍ قَالَ بَلْ سَوَّلَتْ لَكُمْ أَنْفُسُكُمْ أَمْرًا فَصَبْرٌ جَمِيلٌ وَاللَّهُ الْمُسْتَعَانُ عَلَى مَا تَصِفُونَ (١٨))
His saying (عَلَى قَمِيصِهِ): in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الدَّمِ, because the implied form is "they brought false blood on his shirt". And (كَذِبٍ) has the meaning of "possessed of falsehood". It is read, as an irregular (shādhdh) reading, with a dāl [Translator's note: i.e. كَدِبٍ]; الْكَدَبُ is the (white) spots that appear on the nails of young people, and the blood sticking to the shirt was likened to them.
It is also said: الْكَدَبُ means "fresh".
(فَصَبْرٌ جَمِيلٌ): i.e. "so my affair (is beautiful patience)"; the mubtadaʾ (subject) was omitted. If you wish, the omitted element is the khabar (predicate), i.e. "so (beautiful patience) is mine", or "is with me".

ukberi-tibyan:19-19.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَجَاءَتْ سَيَّارَةٌ فَأَرْسَلُوا وَارِدَهُمْ فَأَدْلَى دَلْوَهُ قَالَ يَا بُشْرَى هَذَا غُلَامٌ وَأَسَرُّوهُ بِضَاعَةً وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ (١٩))
His saying (بُشْرَايَ): it is read with a yāʾ with fatḥa after the alif, like عَصَايَ; the yāʾ was given fatḥa only because of the alif.
It is also read without a yāʾ, with an implied ḍamma on the alif, because it is a specifically intended vocative (munādā maqṣūd). It may also be accusative, like His saying (يَا حَسْرَةً عَلَى الْعِبَادِ).
It is also read بُشْرَيَّ with a doubled yāʾ and no alif; this has been mentioned at His saying (هُدًى) in al-Baqara. The meaning is "O glad tidings, be present, for this is your time".
(أَسَرُّوهُ): the fāʿil (agent) is the pronoun of the brothers; it is also said: of the caravan. And «بِضَاعَةً» is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:2-2.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَاهُ قُرْآنًا عَرَبِيًّا لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ (٢))
His saying (قُرْآنًا): in it there are two views:
The first: it is a preparation (tawṭiʾa) for the ḥāl (circumstantial), which is «عَرَبِيًّا». The second: it is a ḥāl, being a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the passive participle, i.e. "collected" or "gathered together"; and «عَرَبِيًّا» is an adjective of it, according to the opinion of those who allow an adjective to be described, or a ḥāl from the pronoun contained in the maṣdar, according to the opinion of those who said that it carries a pronoun when it occupies the place of something that carries a pronoun.

ukberi-tibyan:20-20.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَشَرَوْهُ بِثَمَنٍ بَخْسٍ دَرَاهِمَ مَعْدُودَةٍ وَكَانُوا فِيهِ مِنَ الزَّاهِدِينَ (٢٠))
His saying (بَخْسٍ): a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the passive participle, i.e. مَبْخُوسٍ ("diminished"), or "possessed of diminution". And (دَرَاهِمَ) is a badal (substitute) from ثَمَنٍ.
And (وَكَانُوا فِيهِ مِنَ الزَّاهِدِينَ): the like of it has been mentioned at His saying (وَإِنَّهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ لَمِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ) and (وَنَكُونَ عَلَيْهَا مِنَ الشَّاهِدِينَ).

ukberi-tibyan:21-21.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالَ الَّذِي اشْتَرَاهُ مِنْ مِصْرَ لِامْرَأَتِهِ أَكْرِمِي مَثْوَاهُ عَسَى أَنْ يَنْفَعَنَا أَوْ نَتَّخِذَهُ وَلَدًا وَكَذَلِكَ مَكَّنَّا لِيُوسُفَ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلِنُعَلِّمَهُ مِنْ تَأْوِيلِ الْأَحَادِيثِ وَاللَّهُ غَالِبٌ عَلَى أَمْرِهِ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ (٢١))
His saying (مِنْ مِصْرَ): it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb, as in your saying اشْتَرَيْتُ مِنْ بَغْدَادَ ("I bought from Baghdad"), i.e. in it or at it.
It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الَّذِي» or from the pronoun in «اشْتَرَى», so that it is attached to something omitted.
(وَلِنُعَلِّمَهُ): the lām is attached to something omitted, i.e. "and in order that We teach him, We established him". The like of it has been mentioned at His saying (وَلِتُكْمِلُوا الْعِدَّةَ) and elsewhere. The hāʾ in (أَمْرِهِ) may refer back to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, or to Yūsuf.

ukberi-tibyan:23-23.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَرَاوَدَتْهُ الَّتِي هُوَ فِي بَيْتِهَا عَنْ نَفْسِهِ وَغَلَّقَتِ الْأَبْوَابَ وَقَالَتْ هَيْتَ لَكَ قَالَ مَعَاذَ اللَّهِ إِنَّهُ رَبِّي أَحْسَنَ مَثْوَايَ إِنَّهُ لَا يُفْلِحُ الظَّالِمُونَ (٢٣))
His saying (هَيْتَ لَكَ): in it there are readings. The first: fatḥa on the hāʾ and the tāʾ, with a yāʾ between them. The second: the same, except with kasra on the tāʾ. The third: the same, except with ḍamma on it; these are dialectal forms of it.
The word is a verbal noun (ism fiʿl). Some say it is declarative, meaning "I have made myself ready", and was made indeclinable (mabnī) just as شَتَّانَ was made indeclinable. Others say it is a noun for the imperative, i.e. "come forward" and "come here". Whoever gives it fatḥa seeks lightness; whoever gives it kasra does so because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, like جَيْرِ.
Some give it ḍamma, likening it to حَيْثُ. On this view the lām is for clarification, like the one in their saying سُقْيًا لَكَ ("may you be watered").
The fourth reading: with kasra on the hāʾ, a quiescent hamza and ḍamma on the tāʾ [Translator's note: i.e. هِئْتُ]; on this reading it is a verb from هَاءَ يَهَاءُ, like شَاءَ يَشَاءُ, and يَهِيءُ, like فَاءَ يَفِيءُ. The meaning is "I have made myself ready for you", or "I was created with a fine form for you"; and the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb.
The fifth reading: هُيِّئْتُ لَكَ ("I have been made ready for you"), and it is unusual.
The sixth: with kasra on the hāʾ, sukūn on the hamza and fatḥa on the tāʾ [Translator's note: i.e. هِئْتَ]. The most likely view is that the hamza is a substitute for the yāʾ, or that it is a dialectal form of the word that is a verbal noun, and not a verb; because that would require the address to be to Yūsuf, peace be upon him, which is unsound for two reasons:
The first: he did not make himself ready for her; rather it was she who made herself ready for him. The second: she said «لَكَ», and had the address been intended, it would have been «هِئْتَ لِي».
(قَالَ مَعَاذَ اللَّهِ): it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun); one says عُذْتُ بِهِ عَوْذًا, عِيَاذًا, عِيَاذَةً and مَعَاذًا ("I sought refuge in him").
(إِنَّهُ): the hāʾ is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and the clause after it is the khabar (predicate).

ukberi-tibyan:3-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (نَحْنُ نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ أَحْسَنَ الْقَصَصِ بِمَا أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ هَذَا الْقُرْآنَ وَإِنْ كُنْتَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ لَمِنَ الْغَافِلِينَ (٣))
His saying (أَحْسَنَ): it is accusative in the way a maṣdar (verbal noun) is accusative.
(بِمَا أَوْحَيْنَا): «مَا» is maṣdariyya (forming a maṣdar), «هَذَا» is the object of (أَوْحَيْنَا), and (الْقُرْآنَ) is a naʿt (adjective) of it or an explication (bayān).
In Arabic it would be permissible to put it in the genitive as a badal (substitute) from «مَا», or in the nominative with an implied هُوَ ("it is"). The bāʾ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to نَقُصُّ.
It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from أَحْسَنَ.
The hāʾ in «قَبْلِهِ» refers back to the Qurʾān, or to هَذَا, or to the revealing.

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِذْ قَالَ يُوسُفُ لِأَبِيهِ يَا أَبَتِ إِنِّي رَأَيْتُ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَبًا وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ رَأَيْتُهُمْ لِي سَاجِدِينَ (٤))
His saying (إِذْ قَالَ): i.e. "remember when". In (يُوسُفُ) there are six dialectal forms: ḍamma on the sīn, fatḥa on it, and kasra on it, without a hamza in all of them, and with a hamza in all of them; and يُونُسُ is like it.
(يَا أَبَتِ): it is read with kasra on the tāʾ. The tāʾ in it is an augment, compensating for the yāʾ of the speaker; this is in the vocative specifically. The tāʾ was given kasra to indicate the omitted yāʾ; the two are not combined, so that the compensation and what it compensates for are not combined.
It is also read with fatḥa on it, and in this there are three views. The first: he dropped the tāʾ that compensates for the yāʾ, as the tāʾ of طَلْحَةُ is dropped in curtailment (tarkhīm), and another tāʾ was added in its place and given the vowel of what preceded it, just as they said يَا طَلْحَةَ أَقْبِلْ ("O Ṭalḥa, come"), with fatḥa. The second: he replaced the kasra with a fatḥa, just as an alif is substituted for the yāʾ. The third: he intended يَا «أَبَتَا», as came in poetry:
يَا أَبَتَا عَلَّكَ أَوْ عَسَاكَا
(O my father, perhaps you, or maybe you…)
and the alif was dropped for lightness.
Some permitted ḍamma on the tāʾ, because of its resemblance to the tāʾ of the feminine.
As for pausing on this noun: it is with the tāʾ according to some, because it is not for the feminine, so its form remains as an indication of what was omitted; and with the hāʾ according to others, who likened it to the hāʾ of the feminine. It is also said: the hāʾ is a substitute for the alif that was substituted for the yāʾ. It is also said: it is an augment to make the vowel clear.
And (أَحَدَ عَشَرَ): with fatḥa on the ʿayn according to the original, and with it made quiescent for lightness, to avoid a succession of vowels and to signal the intensity of the fusion (of the two words).
And He repeated «رَأَيْتُ» for emphasis because of the length of the sentence. He made the pronoun in the masculine form because He described them with the attributes of rational beings, namely prostration and obedience; and for that reason He put the adjective in the sound (masculine) plural.
And (سَاجِدِينَ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), because the seeing is seeing with the eye.

ukberi-tibyan:5-5.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ يَا بُنَيَّ لَا تَقْصُصْ رُؤْيَاكَ عَلَى إِخْوَتِكَ فَيَكِيدُوا لَكَ كَيْدًا إِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ لِلْإِنْسَانِ عَدُوٌّ مُبِينٌ (٥))
His saying (رُؤْيَاكَ): the original is with the hamza, and the majority read so. It was also read with a wāw in place of the hamza, because of the ḍamma before it. Among the Arabs are those who assimilate, saying رُيَّاكَ, treating the lightened (wāw) like an original one.
And among them are those who give kasra to the rāʾ to suit the yāʾ. (فَيَكِيدُوا): the answer to the prohibition. (كَيْدًا): in it there are two views. The first: it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the meaning is "so they will devise for you a matter that will plot against you"; it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a noun, and of this is His saying (فَأَجْمِعُوا كَيْدَكُمْ), i.e. "that with which you plot". On this view there are two views concerning the lām. The first: it has the meaning of "for your sake / on your account". The second: it is an adjective placed first, so it became a ḥāl (circumstantial). The other view: it is an emphasizing maṣdar; and on this view there are three views concerning the lām:
The two just mentioned, and the third: it is redundant (zāʾida), because this verb is transitive by itself, and of this is {فَإِن كَانَ لكم كيد فكيدون}.
A parallel to its redundancy here is (رَدِفَ لَكُمْ).

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَكَذَلِكَ يَجْتَبِيكَ رَبُّكَ وَيُعَلِّمُكَ مِنْ تَأْوِيلِ الْأَحَادِيثِ وَيُتِمُّ نِعْمَتَهُ عَلَيْكَ وَعَلَى آلِ يَعْقُوبَ كَمَا أَتَمَّهَا عَلَى أَبَوَيْكَ مِنْ قَبْلُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْحَاقَ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ (٦))
His saying (وَكَذَلِكَ): the kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a choosing like that".
(إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْحَاقَ): two badals (substitutes) from أَبَوَيْكَ.

ukberi-tibyan:7-7.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَقَدْ كَانَ فِي يُوسُفَ وَإِخْوَتِهِ آيَاتٌ لِلسَّائِلِينَ (٧))
His saying (آيَاتٌ): it is read in the plural, because every feature of what happened is a sign.
It is also read in the singular, because all of it is treated as one thing.
It is also said: the singular was put in place of the plural. We have mentioned the origin of (the word) آيَةٌ in al-Baqara.

ukberi-tibyan:9-9.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (اقْتُلُوا يُوسُفَ أَوِ اطْرَحُوهُ أَرْضًا يَخْلُ لَكُمْ وَجْهُ أَبِيكُمْ وَتَكُونُوا مِنْ بَعْدِهِ قَوْمًا صَالِحِينَ (٩))
His saying (أَرْضًا): an adverb (ẓarf) for اطْرَحُوهُ, not a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), because طَرَحَ is not transitive to two objects. It is also said: it is a second object, because اطْرَحُوهُ has the meaning of أَنْزِلُوهُ ("set him down"), and you say أَنْزَلْتُ زَيْدًا الدَّارَ ("I lodged Zayd in the house").
